earlier_scan.note: Extinct Panoan variety known only from a minuscule 1794 wordlist (Palau & Saiz 1989); no phonological description exists.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Reproduces the full 7-word list from Palau & Saiz 1989: 170 (bueno sheoma, malo besoma, el padre reomo, la madre yllquite, el hermano ycoyo, uno tevisí, dos jorová). The two numerals carry written acute accents on the final syllable in the 1794 Spanish-orthography transcription; this is raw data, not a statement about stress.

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99. New York: AMNH. 112 pp.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 12, table 1 note b: 'Chiriba is an otherwise unknown language from Bolivia with a historical list of only seven words, some of which match or resemble word in Panoan languages (and none resemble other languages in the area), particularly Pakawara.. It cannot be classified as Panoan with complete certainty.' p. 96 (appendix 2 sources): '†Chiriba – Palau and Saiz (1989 [Lázaro 1794]: 170) 7-word list'. p. 106: located at Reyes de los Moxos. The 7 words themselves are not reproduced in Fleck.

sources.citation: Hervás y Panduro, Lorenzo. 1800. Catálogo de las lenguas de las naciones conocidas, vol. I: Lenguas y naciones americanas. Madrid: Imprenta de la Administración del Real Arbitrio de Beneficencia. pp. 249-250.

Sole reference: Palau, Mercedes & Blanca Saiz 1989 [1794], type 'a wordlist or less', 16 pp. Ethnologue comment: 'Chiriva, an extinct probably Panoan language of Bolivia attested only with the minuscule wordlist in Palau, Mercedes and Blanca Saiz 1989 [1794]'. AES status extinct. Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology.
